title: Trump Returns to US for Midterm Push, Waves Off Report Tying Chinese Satellite Imagery to Deadly Jordan Strike
detail: President Trump returned to the United States Monday, September 14, 2026, from his Ireland trip, kicking off a stretch of midterm campaigning for Republican candidates as the party's approval numbers sag; NPR's Mara Liasson noted a Quinnipiac poll putting his approval as low as 33%. Asked whether Congress would need to approve the $5,000-per-adult 'Trump dividend' checks he pledged at the Dallas RNC convention, Trump told reporters, 'I don't know. But it's easy enough if the Republicans win, as I said,' offering no further detail on funding mechanics. Separately, speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One, Trump downplayed a Wall Street Journal report that Iran obtained satellite imagery of the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan from Chinese entities before a July 17, 2026 missile strike that killed three US Army soldiers stationed there. 'They basically do what we do. When they say China spies on us, I say you're right and we spy on them too,' Trump said. The Journal report, citing unnamed US officials, did not allege direct Chinese government involvement, and Chinese officials denied the claim. Trump's comments came ahead of his planned September 24 meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, with both governments working to manage trade and geopolitical tensions.

media.caption: Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that the US and China both engage in espionage, downplaying a report on Chinese satellite imagery tied to a deadly attack on US troops in Jordan

title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Bid to Enforce New Mail-Ballot Restrictions for Midterms
detail: The Supreme Court on Monday, September 14, 2026, rejected the Trump administration's emergency request to lift US District Judge Indira Talwani's injunction blocking a new USPS rule — issued under Trump's March 2026 mail-voting executive order — that would have let the Postal Service withhold ballots from voters not on state-supplied eligibility lists and required DHS-approved envelope barcodes, across the 23 states plus D.C. that sued. In an unsigned order, the Court found the administration unlikely to succeed on the merits; Justice Brett Kavanaugh, joined by the majority, wrote that applying the rule to the 2026 elections 'would be arbitrary and capricious in violation of the Administrative Procedure Act' because election officials lack time to implement it before November, while signaling he could rule for the administration if the case returns later. It is the second time in three weeks a court has blocked this specific USPS rule; a separate SCOTUS order on August 24 had lifted a different injunction on the executive order's DHS citizenship-list provisions in the same litigation, leaving the order only partially in effect. Trump reacted on Truth Social, calling the ruling 'a big loss for Republicans, and America itself' that 'makes cheating by the Radical Left "Dumocrats," on Mail-In Ballots, a much easier thing to do,' and criticized his own appointees on the Court.

media.caption: The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's bid to enforce new mail-ballot restrictions ahead of the November midterms

title: Trump Nominates Rep. Wesley Hunt as Ambassador to Saudi Arabia
detail: President Trump on Monday, September 14, 2026, nominated Rep. Wesley Hunt, a second-term Houston Republican and retired Army officer who twice served as a diplomatic liaison in Saudi Arabia, to be US ambassador to Riyadh — filling a post that has sat under interim leadership for nearly the entire second term. Hunt, a West Point graduate, gave up his House seat to run for the Texas Senate seat in 2026 but finished third in the March GOP primary with 13.5% of the vote, behind Attorney General Ken Paxton and Sen. John Cornyn. He has been a Trump ally since endorsing him in 2022 and spoke at the 2024 Republican National Convention; if confirmed, he said he would advance Trump's 'peace through strength' approach and deepen US-Saudi ties. The nomination, sent to the Senate along with several others, faces a tight confirmation window with only about two weeks of Senate floor time remaining before Election Day.

media.caption: Rep. Wesley Hunt was nominated by Trump to be the next US ambassador to Saudi Arabia
